entries.heading: こく‐ふく【克服】
entries.evidence: Daijisen defines effortfully overcoming difficulties and gives illness as an example. Nikkoku includes difficulty-overcoming and a historically sourced enemy-submission formulation; Jitsu glosses bringing under control. Frozen family1285790 gives exact unrestrictedこくふく, transitive noun/suru, and difficulty/illness/crisis overcoming.
entries.decision: Reuse the actual modern difficulty-focused existing article, preserving its N3 level and qualified 'not a general word' territory distinction. Do not turn that practical distinction into an assertion that historical enemy-submission use never existed. Raw服フク metadata and the actual existing non-clothing explanation support the narrow reciprocal example.
entries.limits: Historical coverage does not establish present-day general substitutability or frequency. No expansion of the existing article's selected sense is required; no fresh native-speaker certification.

entries.heading: か・つ【勝・克・贏】
entries.evidence: Actual Nikkoku verb entry identifies intransitive godanかつ; sense④ explicitly marks克 for suppressing hard-to-control desires or forces, and sense⑤ concerns overcoming difficult conditions/illness. Other senses concern competition, gaining and predominance. Daijisen's returned section is a separate nominalized classical勝つ entry, not evidence for the entire modern verb.
entries.decision: Use the actual native reference spelling克つ with kana and a self-control example, supported independently by exact pinned己に克つ family1852770. Preserve rare-spelling flag on standalone克つ in1346150, not a rare-pronunciation claim. No absolute '克 only internal, 勝 only external' rule. Explicit empty quizKunyomi is a practical selection, not denial of documented use.
entries.limits: Only Nikkoku's actually returned verb senses support this interpretation. The general family does not authorize replacing every勝 spelling with克; sense-local restrictions in打ち勝つ remain relevant.
